parts.title: The Sordid Union of Intelligence and Crime: Jeffrey Epstein's Underworld
parts.body: This text explores the sordid union between intelligence and crime that led to Jeffrey Epstein's rise, as detailed in Whitney Webb's book. Epstein's 2019 arrest and suspicious death sparked skepticism, with many believing it protected powerful co-conspirators. Former Labor Secretary Alex Acosta revealed Epstein "had belonged to intelligence," hinting at CIA or Israeli intelligence ties. While mainstream media focused on salacious details, earlier British reports openly discussed Epstein's intelligence connections. His name was even dropped from a major Ponzi scheme investigation, and White House visitor logs showed frequent visits with young women. The book argues that Epstein was not an anomaly but part of a century-long pattern of sexual blackmail for intelligence gathering, rooted in the cooperation between organized crime and intelligence, epitomized by Operation Underworld in WWII. This alliance has created a covert power structure using blackmail, bribes, and assassinations to control institutions and manipulate the public.

parts.title: The Intertwined History of Western Economic Interests, Organized Crime, and the Global Drug Trade
parts.body: This text explores the historical connections between Western economic interests, organized crime, and the global drug trade, particularly focusing on China and the activities leading up to and during World War II. It details how monopoly authorities added significant taxes to opium, making its original cost a fraction of the final price. Key figures like Arnold Rothstein, mentor to notorious mobsters Lansky, Luciano, and Costello, dispatched frontmen to China, initiating a lucrative global narcotics network. These figures, including Sidney Stajer, Jacob Katzenberg, and George Uffner, often had deep ties to New York City's Jewish crime syndicates, which controlled much of the city's heroin distribution. The narrative further reveals the complicity of Western economic interests, especially the powerful Sassoon family, in the Chinese opium trade. Nicknamed the “Rothschilds of the East,” the Sassoons dominated a significant portion of the opium trade, making them immensely wealthy and major real estate owners in Shanghai. Their interests, along with those of Jardine-Matheson and the Keswick family, became deeply intertwined, extending into the oil industry and influencing international drug trade and the evolution of Western intelligence services. This history highlights a complex web where corporate power, organized crime, and global politics converged to shape illicit economies.

parts.title: Booze and Blackmail: The Bronfmans and the Underworld
parts.body: This chapter, "Booze and Blackmail," explores the rise of the Bronfman family in the liquor industry, from their humble beginnings as Jewish immigrants fleeing persecution in Bessarabia to becoming major players in North America. Initially, the family, led by Samuel Bronfman, ventured into the hotel business in Canada, which faced accusations of violating liquor laws and condoning gambling. Their fortunes dramatically shifted with the advent of Prohibition in Canada and later the United States, which they exploited through loopholes and strategic alliances, leading them to become prominent bootleggers. Key to their success were early ties to the Hudson's Bay Company and subsequently to major British distillers, securing exclusive import rights and establishing their own distilleries like Seagram's. The Bronfman's illicit operations extended across the Canadian-US border, the Caribbean, and Mexico, making immense profits by degrading imported liquor and shipping it back to the US. Despite facing charges for conspiracy and tax evasion, they were acquitted, settling for a fraction of their gains, and maintaining a cozy, albeit discreet, relationship with figures of the National Crime Syndicate, including Meyer Lansky. The narrative also delves into the lives of the Bronfmans' "middlemen" like Joseph Reinfeld and Lewis Rosenstiel. Reinfeld was crucial for dealing with crime-linked individuals and laundering profits, often bringing the Bronfmans into contact with mobsters like Longy Zwillman. His testimony before the Kefauver Committee revealed the family's illicit activities and even suggested their hotels were brothels. Rosenstiel, initially a partner, became a bitter rival of Samuel Bronfman. His rise in the liquor industry, particularly with Schenley Distillers Company, is shrouded in a sanitized official narrative, omitting his significant ties to organized crime figures like Meyer Lansky and Frank Costello. Rosenstiel's notorious use of blackmail, including bugging his offices and home, and his alleged involvement in a sex extortion ring with Roy Cohn and J. Edgar Hoover at the Plaza Hotel, highlights a dark side. These revelations suggest a deeply intertwined relationship between organized crime, powerful individuals, and even government agencies, with Hoover himself potentially being blackmailed, which influenced his reluctance to tackle organized crime as FBI director.

parts.title: The Intertwined Worlds of Hoover, Rosenstiel, and Cohn
parts.body: This section reveals the complex connections between J. Edgar Hoover, Lewis Rosenstiel, and Roy Cohn, linking them to organized crime networks and blackmail. Hoover's relationship with Rosenstiel reportedly began in the 1950s, possibly earlier, with evidence suggesting Hoover's unusual concern for Rosenstiel's criminal ties in 1939. The mysterious ease with which Roy Cohn, a young man in his mid-20s, gained a personal audience with Hoover in 1952 has puzzled biographers, leading to speculation that their connection might have stemmed from the same hidden networks and "blue suite" parties that linked Hoover and Rosenstiel. This early, seemingly improbable, access hints at a deeper, unacknowledged bond between these powerful figures. The unusual closeness among Rosenstiel, Cohn, and Hoover extended beyond their initial meetings, manifesting in mutual favors, compliments, and gifts. Their shared commitment to anti-communism was the official explanation, but the context of secretive orgies and blackmail suggests a stronger, more personal bond. Key events include Hoover sending flowers to Rosenstiel, Rosenstiel's declaration of "Your wish is my command" to Hoover, and the hiring of Hoover's "Number 2," Louis B. Nichols, by Rosenstiel's Schenley company. Rosenstiel also notably purchased 25,000 copies of Hoover's book, *Masters of Deceit*, for distribution to schools. The formation of the J. Edgar Hoover Foundation in 1965, heavily funded by Rosenstiel and with Cohn's American Jewish League Against Communism contributing, further highlights their interconnectedness. The foundation's unusual inactivity in its early years, as noted by a 1969 *Washington Post* report, adds to the intrigue surrounding these relationships. As Rosenstiel retired, he sold his Manhattan townhouse, allegedly bugged for blackmail, to Meshulam Riklis, a figure whose rise was viewed with skepticism and who later absorbed Schenley into his Rapid-American Corporation.

parts.title: Louis Mortimer Bloomfield, Permindex-CMC, and Covert Global Networks
parts.body: The provided text delves into Permindex-CMC, a mysterious entity in Rome tied to American, Italian, French, and Israeli intelligence networks, as well as international organized criminal actors and their banks. It highlights Louis Mortimer Bloomfield's role as Permindex's attorney, coordinating various players across continents and effectively hiding their identities by holding stock in his name. The text details Permindex-CMC's origins, including its initial purpose as a world trade center and its later connections to covert networks, including the CIA and Mossad. Key figures like Gershon Peres (Shimon Peres's brother) and Clay Shaw (a CIA contract agent) are mentioned as having been on the board. The text also outlines Bloomfield's ties to various Zionist organizations, his communication with British spymaster William Stephenson, and his later correspondence with George H.W. Bush. Further, the document reveals deep involvement of Tibor Rosenbaum and his International Credit Bank with Permindex-CMC, particularly through the real estate holding company Marina Reale. Investors in Marina Reale included Dov Biegun of the World Zionist Organization and Nate Dolin, who had business ties to mobster Moe Dalitz. The text uncovers the involvement of Compagnie Financière (now the Edmond de Rothschild Group) in Permindex-CMC's real estate ventures, with Edmond de Rothschild himself being a business partner of Rosenbaum in the Israel Corporation. Connections to the oil industry are also explored, with Israel Continental Oil and Tri-Continental Pipelines showing intertwined interests among figures like Rothschild, Francois Pereire, and Louis Bloomfield, often linked to organized crime and the development of Israel's economy. The document discusses the controversial death of Enrico Mattei, head of ENI, and allegations linking his death to Permindex and the OAS, as well as potential money laundering activities through IAHC and BNL.

parts.title: Roy Cohn's Rise and Early Controversies
parts.body: This text details Roy Cohn's early life and career, including his family's history of mental health issues and his mother's permissive parenting, which shaped his character. Cohn was known for his "human calculus" skills from a young age, using his father's connections and forming friendships with influential people like Si Newhouse Jr. and Generoso (Gene) Pope Jr., who later became media magnates. Pope Sr., a powerful figure with ties to Italian fascism, the Vatican, and mobsters like Frank Costello (who became Gene Jr.'s godfather), mentored Cohn in "practical politics" and the "favor bank" system. Cohn's connections helped him secure an assistant attorney position under Irving Saypol, leading to his role in the Rosenberg trial and the McCarthy hearings. His close relationship with J. Edgar Hoover secured his appointment as McCarthy's chief counsel, where he played a key role in the "Red" and "Lavender" scares. Cohn's attempt to blackmail the Army for preferential treatment for his rumored lover, David Schine, ultimately led to his and McCarthy's downfall during the Army-McCarthy hearings. The text also highlights Cohn's use of blackmail against diplomats and his involvement with sexual blackmail operations linked to the anti-Communist "hunt" and the "lavender scare."

parts.title: Intertwined Worlds: Finance, Organized Crime, and the CIA
parts.body: In the early 1950s, Fox led a CIA front in Indonesia, the American-Indonesian Corporation, controlling rights to natural resources and government transactions with the US. He also covertly supported the CIA-backed prime minister, Mohammed Hatta. Around the same time, Sonny Fassoulis acquired Bon Ami stock from Guterma, using film rights as payment, aiming to exchange an "Icthyan Package" for television spot time. Fassoulis and Fox were linked to a shadowy financial network involving Virgil Dardi years earlier. Fox chaired Pola-Lite (a subsidiary of intelligence-linked Commerce International Corporation, run by Fassoulis) and was president of C & C Television Corporation, where Dardi was a director. During the United Dye scandal in the early 1960s, an investigation targeted the David, Josephine and Winfield Baird Foundation and the Lansing Foundation, controlled by David Baird. The Baird Foundation owned a significant stake in C & C Television Corporation and its subsidiaries, and its clients included organized crime associates like Louis Chesler, William Zeckendorf, and Lawrence Wien (linked to the Desert Inn and United Dye case). Nathan Cummings, a director of Bon Ami, was involved in its sale to United Dye when controlled by Guterma and Dardi. Baird and Charles Allen of Allen & Co. had dealings with Guterma, even after the Las Vegas mob had moved on. Louis Mortimer Bloomfield (attorney for Permindex) noted Baird's interest in Permindex's affairs. Baird's banker, Serge Semenenko (VP of First National Bank of Boston), had close ties to the CIA. The Baird Foundation itself was later revealed to be a CIA asset, receiving significant funds for Middle East and Africa programs. Baird also had connections to Meshulam Riklis, who acquired Stanley Warner Corp. and, later, Lewis Rosenstiel’s Schenley Industries, with Baird receiving a large finder’s fee. These interconnected financial activities highlight a complex web of organized crime figures, businessmen, and intelligence agencies involved in blackmail and power plays.

parts.title: The Radford-Moorer Affair and the Roots of Watergate
parts.body: The text delves into the Radford-Moorer affair, revealing a complex web of espionage and political intrigue surrounding Nixon and Kissinger's secret diplomatic efforts to open relations with China. Yeoman Charles Radford, connected to journalist Jack Anderson, was found to be pilfering highly confidential documents regarding these initiatives. These documents were allegedly passed to Admiral Welander and Admiral Moorer, who then used them to undermine Kissinger's foreign policy. Moorer, with ties to the John Birch Society and the China Lobby, was against the China initiative and used these leaks to his advantage. The text also explores the question of who leaked information to Anderson, suggesting it might have been Welander or Moorer themselves, possibly using Radford as a scapegoat. Anderson's own ties to the China Lobby and figures like Anna Chennault are highlighted, implying his column may have been weaponized by powerful factions before. The narrative further connects this to the Watergate scandal, indicating that key figures had foreknowledge of the events. The groundwork for Watergate is then explored, detailing how William Haddad tried to warn DNC officials about a planned burglary. The interconnectedness of private investigators, security firms, and CIA operatives is emphasized, showing a dense network of individuals, many with backgrounds in anti-Castro operations, involved in the lead-up to the Watergate break-ins. The text suggests that the bungled burglary might have been a deliberate setup or a controlled demolition of the Nixon administration.

parts.title: The 1982 Capitol Hill Drug and Sex Scandal
parts.body: The text discusses a drug ring operating on Capitol Hill, initially reported by CBS Evening News in 1982. Key figures like Douglas Marshall, Robert Finkel, and Troy Todd were arrested for cocaine possession, with Marshall and Finkel charged with distribution. Devon Dupres, described as a "Georgetown cocktail waitress" and an assistant to a discotheque owner, was an unindicted co-conspirator. The ring involved congressional pages, tour guides, and other Hill employees, with Marshall himself being a former page and Finkel an elevator operator. Jack Anderson reported that over 15 members of Congress were customers, and publicly linked the drug ring to prostitution and sexual abuse allegations involving pages. An FBI investigation and a House Ethics Committee inquiry were launched, led by Joseph Califano. Richard Powers and John "Jack" Moriarty, former police officers, were investigators. An anonymous tip led them to Robert Keith Gray, and DC police officer Carl Shoffler provided extensive information on Gray's alleged ties to Edwin Wilson and the CIA, drug involvement, and orgies. Shoffler also claimed a male prostitution service on Capitol Hill was linked to a consultant for Diamond Shamrock, a client of Gray & Co. Michael Pilgrim and Neil Livingstone (who worked for Gray & Co. and had intelligence ties) then contacted Shoffler, raising suspicions. Later, Gray's attorney, Thomas Fortuin (who was also Tony Salerno's lawyer), offered Shoffler an interview and implied Moriarty had leaked information to Gray's associates, suggesting a conflict of interest. Shoffler reported an attempted bribe, leading to a Department of Justice investigation. Powers and Moriarty were suspended by Califano amidst the probe. The investigation concluded with more questions than answers, as the US Capitol Police were found to have destroyed documents related to drug trafficking. Allegations of sexual abuse and homosexual prostitution were dismissed after page Leroy Williams recanted, claiming he fabricated the story, even though the implicated Congressman, Larry Craig, later had his own scandal.

parts.title: Covert Networks and Financial Intrigue: The Cold War Underbelly
parts.body: This text delves into a complex web of financial dealings, intelligence operations, and political maneuvering during the Cold War era, particularly focusing on the United States, the Middle East, and Africa. Key figures like William Casey, George H.W. Bush, and Robert Vesco are highlighted for their involvement in shadowy networks. The Safari Club, a covert intelligence alliance, played a significant role in countering Soviet influence, with Saudi Arabia, France, Egypt, Morocco, and Iran as members. The Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) served as its financial vehicle, entangled in money laundering and other illicit activities. The narrative also explores the intricate connections between oil interests, banking, and intelligence agencies, often overlapping with organized crime. The text further examines "Billygate," a scandal involving President Jimmy Carter's brother, Billy, and his ties to Libya. This affair was allegedly manipulated by Israeli intelligence and the "private CIA" network to destabilize Carter's administration. Connections between the DuPont family's financial empire, the Teamsters Union, and figures like Armand Hammer and Robert Vesco illustrate the pervasive influence of these interconnected networks. The ongoing investigation into Vesco's activities, including his alleged involvement in drug trafficking and arms deals, continued to expose the deep corruption and political intrigue of the period.

parts.title: Intertwined Worlds: Business, Intelligence, and Organized Crime in the 1970s and 80s
parts.body: The text details the interconnectedness of various powerful figures, organizations, and clandestine operations during the 1970s and 80s, highlighting a web of business, intelligence, and organized crime. Mohamed al-Fayed's conflict with Lonrho revealed allegations of arms dealing involving ex-CIA agent Edwin Wilson and a Lonrho subsidiary, Tradewinds, which had a Libyan security chief as a director. Lonrho's chairman, Edward du Cann, had ties to Robert Vesco, who was involved in Libyan business affairs during the Carter administration, intersecting with Shackley's group. Further connections are drawn to Charter Oil, partly owned by Carl Lindner (a Republican supporter and associate of Max Fisher, who mentored Leslie Wexner). The document then shifts to William Casey's legal career before becoming CIA director, showcasing his clients' links to intelligence and organized crime. Deak & Co., run by OSS veteran Nicholas Deak, handled CIA funds and was implicated in money laundering for South American drug financiers. Casey also represented companies controlled by Victor Posner, a corporate raider tied to Michael Milken and Ivan Boesky (whose defense was supported by Max Fisher). Posner's associate, Armer E. White, had deep connections to organized crime through real estate, involving figures like Leonard Pelullo and the Scarfo crime family. Another Casey client, SCA Services, a waste-management company, had mob ties involving Anthony Bentrovato and the Teamsters pension fund, and was linked to the Genovese crime family. Frank Walsh, a close associate of Leslie Wexner, was also investigated for ties to these same organized crime networks, with his business address notably being Wexner's company. Finally, the text explores John Shaheen, an oilman and OSS veteran, who, with Casey, became involved with Cyrus Hashemi, an Iranian arms dealer, leading into the October Surprise plot and alleged meetings in Madrid involving Casey and Iranian officials to discuss the hostage crisis.

parts.title: The Rise and Fall of BCCI: A Global Nexus of Illicit Finance and Intelligence
parts.body: The Bank of Commerce and Credit International (BCCI), founded in 1972, was a powerful but illicit financial institution, described by TIME as the “dirtiest bank of them all.” Its founder, Agha Hasan Abedi, an economic advisor to Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, envisioned it as a global bank for the third world. However, with backing from the Saudi royal family and potentially the CIA, BCCI became a hub for money laundering, capital flight, and fraud. Allegations suggest the CIA, specifically Richard Helms, was involved in its creation to provide cover for intelligence operations. BCCI operated a "black network" involved in arms trade, drug and gold transport, sex trafficking, and murder-for-hire. It supported A.Q. Khan's Pakistani nuclear weapons program and facilitated financial ties between Pakistan and the Persian Gulf through migrant remittances, which also inflated its balance sheets. Additionally, BCCI was implicated in sex trafficking, including minors, through figures like Sani Ahmad. BCCI aimed to penetrate the US financial system, initially courting American Express, then forming a significant partnership with Bank of America, which later sold its shares due to concerns, though still maintaining correspondent relations. A major US entry point was through Bert Lance, a prominent banker and friend of President Jimmy Carter, who, despite scandals, facilitated BCCI's acquisition of Financial General Bankshares (FGB). Notable figures involved included Jackson Stephens, Armand Hammer, and eventually, key BCCI operatives like Kamal Adham. The acquisition was fraught with legal battles, but with the help of lawyers Clark Clifford and Robert Altman, BCCI eventually gained control, renaming FGB to First American Bankshares. This process involved multiple dummy companies and allegedly, the complicity of the Federal Reserve and the White House. BCCI also cultivated relationships with US politicians, including Jimmy Carter, and was a major donor to his Presidential Center and the Global 2000 project. Other connections included the Chiefs of Police National Drug Task Force and figures like Robert Keith Gray and Ghaith Pharaon, who maintained significant political ties and involvement in other questionable financial dealings, including with Khalid bin Mahfouz and James R. Bath, a reported CIA asset linked to George H.W. Bush and Saudi investments.

parts.title: Murdoch's Media Empire and GMT's Shady Connections in Iran-Contra
parts.body: The Iran-Contra scandal revealed Rupert Murdoch as a key media ally for a propaganda campaign, becoming close to the Reagan White House. This alliance greatly benefited Murdoch, allowing him to expand his US media holdings and create Fox Broadcasting Corporation in 1987. Simultaneously, Richard Singlaub served as a consultant for GeoMiliTech Consultants Corporation (GMT), a Florida-based company potentially set up at his suggestion. GMT worked with arms dealers like Ernest Werner Glaft and Samuel Cummings, a long-time weapons merchant for the CIA whose brother-in-law, Senator John Tower, later oversaw the Iran-Contra inquiry, creating a major conflict of interest. GMT had close ties to Israel, with its executive vice president Ron Harel being a veteran of the Israeli Air Force and its overseas offices located in Tel Aviv. A sister company, Global Technologies Ltd., also in Israel, was overseen by Joel Arnon, an Israeli diplomat and GMT vice president. Shaul Eisenberg, an Israeli billionaire with close ties to Israeli intelligence, owned the building housing Global Technologies. GMT also used Israel Discount Bank, where funds for other operations were deposited. Remarkably, GMT was linked to the clandestine activities of Robert Maxwell and his network, particularly through Nicholas Davies, foreign editor of Maxwell’s *Daily Mirror*. Davies, like Maxwell, was alleged to work for Mossad, using his journalism as a cover for arms trafficking. Davies also managed the Ora Group, an Israeli company in London that facilitated arms flows, including Soviet bloc weapons, to clients like GMT. Internal documents showcased Davies's role in these affairs. Davies denied these claims, but journalists refuted his counter-allegations. GMT also utilized offshore banking, with its principals setting up Consulentia Ltd. to hide its existence. GMT was involved in acquiring arms for the Contras in 1985 and was part of discussions for a complex three-way trading scheme involving the US, Israel, and China to fund covert operations and exchange arms for technology. While this plan was officially never completed, elements of it, such as increased US-Israel-China economic and political relations and their collaboration in arming the Mujahideen in Afghanistan, did materialize. Notably, Jeffrey Epstein was later implicated in similar arms deals involving the Mujahideen. GMT was also involved in early arms deals with Iran, predating the Enterprise's formation, through a swap of tanks for F-14 fighter aircraft, with Israel acting as a cut-out.

parts.title: Kissinger's Networks: BCCI, Iraq, and the Shultz Connection
parts.body: This text delves into money-laundering schemes and high-technology transfers to the Eastern Bloc, focusing on the intricate connections of Henry Kissinger. Kissinger's personal ties to George P. Shultz, formed during the Nixon administration, are highlighted, with Kissinger stating he would choose Shultz for president. Shultz reportedly consulted Kissinger on Middle East policy, likely including Iraq. A significant network connected Kissinger Associates to Bechtel through William E. Simon, who also had ties to the Gouletas family (linked to Jeffrey Epstein), Covenant House, AmeriCares, and Saudi investor Suliman Olayan. Simon's long history with Kissinger and his role as Shultz's successor as Nixon's Treasury Secretary suggest a deep-seated "affectionate comradeship." This extensive network, including BNL and BCCI, is portrayed as actively aiding Iraq against Iran, even seemingly working both sides of the conflict by supplying arms to both nations. The text suggests the Bofors-led powder cartel and the Enterprise were just parts of a larger international web of money laundering, backroom deals, and arms trafficking. The text then details the unresolved ties of Kissinger Associates to BCCI. In 1986, Sergio de Costa, a Kissinger Associates consultant, lobbied for BCCI to become a client, finding an ally in Alan Stoga, former chief economist at First National Bank of Chicago (linked to Rockefeller interests). Stoga reportedly attended a 1987 meeting with BNL, where Lawrence Eagleburger was also present, and had extensive contact with BCCI principals. While Kissinger Associates claimed Stoga pushed for the client relationship with Kissinger being reticent, BCCI's files indicated that Stoga continued to meet with them even after Kissinger Associates claimed talks had ended, with the door for a relationship remaining open. Although a direct working relationship was never cemented, Kissinger Associates unofficially recommended BCCI to the New York law firm of Arnold & Porter, where William D. Rogers, who had served under Kissinger and helped set up Kissinger Associates, was a partner. This entire narrative suggests a complex interplay of personal connections and corporate interests in the murky world of international finance and geopolitics.

parts.title: Mena Operations and Clinton's Early Connections
parts.body: The Mena airport in Arkansas saw new activity with Australian companies Southern Cross Aviation Inc. and Multi-Trade. Southern Cross, an aircraft ferrying company specializing in C-130s, and Multi-Trade, an aircraft interiors business, shared principals who were interested in the planes stored at Mena. One executive, Glen Conrad, sold his stake in a C-130 to African Air Trans Inc., a company owned by Henry A. Warton, a pilot and smuggler with CIA ties. This C-130, involved in arms trafficking, was later seized by US Customs. Another C-130 linked to Mena crashed in Angola, killing Chuck Hendricks, an Arkansas mechanic. This plane was owned by CZX Productions and leased by Unitrann International, both controlled by Dietrich Reinhardt. Reinhardt's company, St. Lucia Airways, was a CIA proprietary firm used to ferry weapons during the Iran-Contra affair, suggesting ongoing operations at Mena. Hot Springs, Arkansas, had a long history as a hub for organized crime. There's circumstantial evidence that a young Bill Clinton had contact with these elements through his uncle, Raymond Clinton, a car dealer with underworld ties and political influence. Raymond helped Bill secure a draft deferral for Vietnam and provided financial support for his early political campaigns, including a loan for his 1974 House race and contributions to his 1978 gubernatorial campaign. Hints suggest Clinton might have also been a CIA informant during his time at Oxford, supplying information on activist groups in exchange for draft insurance. Barry Seal, an affiliate of Oliver North, was involved in Contra-connected operations near Mena. Former Arkansas policeman L.D. Brown, Clinton's driver, claimed Clinton encouraged him to join the CIA and edited his essay on drug smuggling in Central America, leading to Brown's contact with Seal. Terry Reed, another North associate, established a training base near Mena for Nicaraguan Contras. Dan Lasater, a well-connected Little Rock bond broker, was linked to Seal and the Arkansas cocaine world, a world shared with Roger Clinton, Bill's brother, who worked for Lasater. Lasater's ski resort in New Mexico was also a center for drug running and money laundering, with reports of strange nighttime traffic and military-type cargo planes reminiscent of Mena.

parts.title: The Shadowy World of Robert Maxwell: From War Refugee to Media Mogul and Intelligence Asset
parts.body: This chapter, "High Tech Treason: The Making of a Maxwell," details the complex and shadowy life of Robert Maxwell, born Jan Ludvick Hoch, who adopted several aliases before settling on "Robert Maxwell." He served in the British military during WWII and was befriended by Count Frederich vanden Huevel, an associate of Allen Dulles. Maxwell's family perished in the Holocaust, and he leveraged post-war contacts to build a media empire with Pergamon Press as its cornerstone. This attracted the attention of various intelligence agencies, including British, Russian, and Israeli services. Despite early attempts by MI6 to recruit him, a background check revealed his loyalty was "only to Israel." He was formally recruited by Israeli intelligence in the early 1960s, using his access to prominent businessmen and world leaders to his advantage. Maxwell's political ambitions led him to the British Parliament in 1964, though his re-election bid failed. He later faced a government inquiry into his management of Pergamon Press, which concluded he was not a "person who can be relied on to exercise proper stewardship." Undeterred, Maxwell reacquired control and began to develop deep ties to powerful figures like Margaret Thatcher, Shaul Eisenberg, Edmund Safra, Henry Kissinger, and George H.W. Bush. Maxwell's influence extended globally, fostering relationships with dictators and intelligence officials in Eastern Europe and the Soviet Union, including Semion Mogilevich of the Russian mafia, for whom Maxwell secured Israeli passports to facilitate access to US financial institutions. His media empire expanded significantly, acquiring British Printing Corporation (renamed Maxwell Communication Corporation), the Mirror Group, and later MacMillan and the New York Daily News. Allegedly, funds from his companies were "borrowed" to finance Mossad activities, a system he later disrupted by using the funds for personal lavishness and further business expansion. His ties to Israeli intelligence deepened, particularly with Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir, who harbored negative sentiments towards the US, potentially influencing Israel's more aggressive espionage targeting the US, with Maxwell as a key figure.

parts.title: Suspicious Deaths, Intertwined Companies, and Intelligence Connections
parts.body: This text discusses the suspicious circumstances surrounding Vince Foster's death and its link to Jeffrey Epstein's early visits to the Clinton White House. It also delves into E-Systems, a defense contractor specializing in computer software, and its alleged close ties to Systematics and the Inslaw affair. Authors like James Norman and J. Orlin Grabbe suggest that sensitive E-Systems computer code ended up in Israel shortly after its NSA deployment. The company also had tight connections with Wackenhut, sharing board members like William Raborn. E-Systems, originating as LTV Electrosystems, maintained a cozy relationship with the CIA and other intelligence agencies, often operating under confidentiality agreements. CIA officials considered them "automatic hires" for E-Systems, highlighting their intertwined nature. Notable collaborations include constructing ground stations in China for eavesdropping on Soviet satellites and purchasing Air Asia, a CIA proprietary airline. E-Systems also became involved in Operation Condor, a DEA-supported Mexican government initiative against drug trade, where they provided maintenance for Evergreen's planes. The text then shifts to Robert Booth Nichols, a key figure in the PROMIS scandal with alleged ties to organized crime, including the Gambino family and Yakuza, and money laundering for Ferdinand Marcos. Nichols served on the board of FIDCO, a supposed NSC corporate cut-out for financing reconstruction in Lebanon, where PROMIS software was encountered. He also co-founded Meridian Arms, involved in Cabazon activities with Wackenhut. Eugene Gianquinto of MCA, also linked to Meridian, allegedly used his influence to quash a DOJ probe into MCA's organized crime ties. Nichols's connections extended to a US Senator for drug trafficking and money laundering, with Senator Howard Baker being a potential suspect due to his MCA board membership and later business with Robert Maxwell. Journalist Danny Casolaro, investigating a global criminal syndicate he called "the Octopus" that encompassed the PROMIS scandal, Iran-Contra, and BCCI, was threatened by Nichols and found dead shortly after, ruled a suicide amidst much controversy and missing evidence. The article also mentions the suspicious deaths of other individuals connected to the PROMIS scandal, including Robert Maxwell and John Tower, and William Barr's alleged role in stonewalling Congress regarding the Inslaw affair and appointing a special counsel whose report was widely criticized as a "whitewash."

parts.title: Government by Blackmail: The Dark Secrets of the Reagan Era
parts.body: The chapter explores the alliance between intelligence networks and organized crime, highlighting how it fueled business rackets and criminal elements during the Reagan era. Key scandals like Iran-Contra, PROMIS, and BCCI, initially seen as isolated, are presented as routine for the period, protected by high-level government figures, including William Barr, who allegedly covered up these affairs. The narrative suggests a deeper level of corruption, reaching the White House, where sex blackmail, organized crime, and personal gain intertwined with intelligence agendas. Prominent figures in this milieu included Roy Cohn, a lawyer with strong ties to organized crime, media moguls, and political power. Cohn's "favor bank" system, leveraging his connections with figures like Donald Trump, Rupert Murdoch, and Barbara Walters, enabled him to become a major "political fixer" for the Republican Party, particularly during Reagan's campaigns. His close relationships extended to Reagan's inner circle, including William Casey and Nancy Reagan, highlighting the deep integration of these networks within the highest echelons of power. The chapter also touches upon the connections between Cohn and figures involved in the Franklin Scandal and AmeriCares, further illustrating the widespread nature of these interconnected criminal enterprises.

parts.title: Larry King's Network: Abuse, Blackmail, and Craig Spence's Alleged CIA Ties
parts.body: This document details Larry King's network and its alleged involvement in sadistic physical and sexual abuse, including whippings, knife wounds, and cigarette burns. Witnesses claimed seeing kidnapped children, some as young as twelve, at King’s “parties” and “orgies.” One even described a child’s molestation, torture, and murder being filmed. While King was based in Omaha, he was also active in Washington DC, where he had a lavish residence. King’s DC activities were linked to Craig Spence, a lobbyist known for throwing lavish parties attended by influential figures from politics, media, and government. Spence's parties, which sometimes included cocaine and underage escorts, were bugged with recording equipment and two-way mirrors to blackmail guests. parts.title: Jeffrey Epstein, The Clinton White House, Big Tech, and the Evolution of Blackmail
parts.body: The Epstein-Maxwell saga extends beyond sex trafficking, delving into espionage activities and Jeffrey Epstein's unusual ties to the Clinton White House (1993-1995). Epstein had 17 known White House meetings, often bringing young, attractive women. Many meetings were with Mark Middleton, who died under suspicious circumstances in 2022 and was involved in foreign espionage investigated by Congress. This suggests a major, uninvestigated scandal of the Clinton era. Volume 2 also explores the Epstein/Maxwells' connections to Big Tech, particularly Microsoft executives like Bill Gates and Nathan Myhrvold, and the Maxwell siblings' intelligence ties and influence in Big Tech, linked to the stolen PROMIS software (Volume 1). The book concludes that blackmail has evolved with technology, moving from individuals like Epstein to mass surveillance systems. This shift may explain why Epstein and the Maxwells began targeting Silicon Valley figures after Epstein's first arrest, and his investments in data harvesting and mass surveillance firms. The ultimate result is a society where power structures control information for wealth and control, making the US "one nation under blackmail" rather than "one nation under God." Whitney Webb, 8/23/22.

parts.title: From Leese to Hoffenberg
parts.body: In 1987, Douglas Leese introduced Jeffrey Epstein to Steven Jude Hoffenberg, founder of Towers Financial Corporation, a collection agency that became much more with Epstein's help. Hoffenberg claims Leese, a principal at Towers, wanted him to hire Epstein for securities sales and for the purpose of embezzlement and fraud. While Hoffenberg took the fall for these crimes, he alleged that Douglas Leese and his sons Julian and Nicholas were also involved. Hoffenberg described Epstein as a "genius" at selling securities with "no moral compass." Both Epstein and Hoffenberg were involved in a massive Ponzi scheme through Towers Financial, siphoning funds from insurance companies and selling unregistered promissory notes to ordinary people. They became very close, with Hoffenberg calling Epstein his "best friend" and "wingman." Despite later claims of firing Epstein for stealing, Hoffenberg maintained connections to Epstein/Maxwell networks, using the same lawyers as Robert Maxwell for his New York Post acquisition. When Towers Financial collapsed, Hoffenberg testified that Epstein was in charge of the fraudulent transactions, yet Epstein's name mysteriously disappeared from the case and he was never charged.

parts.title: Jeffrey Epstein's Connections and Real Estate Network
parts.body: The chapter details the complex and often controversial connections of Jeffrey Epstein, particularly with Donald Trump and various real estate figures. Trump and Epstein knew each other for years, with Epstein attending parties at Trump's properties and even claiming to have introduced Trump to Melania. Despite Trump calling Epstein a "terrific guy" in 2002 and saying he liked "beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side," their friendship reportedly ended in 2004 over a Palm Beach property rivalry. Trump later distanced himself from Epstein after his 2019 arrest but offered well wishes to Ghislaine Maxwell after her arrest. Epstein's contact books also listed Trump, Melania, and the Trilateral Commission, and Epstein was a high-level donor to the Council on Foreign Relations, which only revoked his membership for "nonpayment of dues" after his first arrest, not the conviction itself. The narrative then shifts to Epstein’s extensive real estate web and his connection to Leslie Wexner. Wexner-linked entities, with Epstein as vice president and treasurer of Parkview Financial (formerly Lewex), shared office space in the Huntington Center, a building controlled by Gerald D. Hines, whose ventures were intertwined with figures like Walter Mischer, the Bush family, and Adnan Khashoggi, all with intelligence connections. This arrangement raised questions, especially given Epstein's own alleged intelligence ties. Parkview Financial, particularly after the "Shapiro murder," became a crucial vehicle for Wexner's and Epstein's real estate dealings in NYC, expanding holdings like Dara Gardens. The financing for Dara Gardens came from Dime Savings Bank, which had ties to the Rockefeller family through its top executive Richard Parsons. Myles J. Horn, president of Imperial Properties, managed Dara Gardens and was later arrested for attempting to bribe the Trump-owned Taj Mahal casino. Ossa Properties, owned by Epstein's brother Mark, was involved in managing Dara Gardens and other properties, like 301 East 66th Street, which was allegedly used to "house underage girls" from foreign countries and was frequented by Ehud Barak, former Israeli Prime Minister, who received a large grant from the Wexner Foundation. The chapter also details the sale of 11 East 71st Street from Epstein to the Comet Trust, whose trustee, Guido Goldman, had close ties to Henry Kissinger and served as a CIA liaison to the Council on Foreign Relations. The chapter concludes by discussing Epstein's rental of a State Department-owned mansion on East 69th Street, subletting it to lawyer Ivan Fisher, which raised questions about Epstein's initial connection to the State Department and Secretary James Baker III, who had ties to figures like Raymond Hill and his S&L, which was linked to Adnan Khashoggi and intelligence networks.

parts.title: Max Fisher: Oil Tycoon to Political Powerhouse
parts.body: Max Fisher, a prominent figure in the United Jewish Appeal and chief fundraiser for Michigan Governor George Romney, consistently downplayed his success, attributing it to being "in the right place at the right time." He famously gambled on the expansion of the oil industry post-WWII, which led his company, Aurora Gasoline, to a $39 million buyout by Ohio Oil (later Marathon Oil) in 1959. Fisher, holding 38% of the stock, netted $13,870,000. After retiring from oil, he shifted his focus to public life and expanding his influence, particularly in Detroit, serving on numerous boards including the Detroit Economic Club and the Detroit Institute of Arts. Fisher then moved into real estate development in Detroit, notably initiating the Detroit Renaissance Center and Riverside West. He frequently partnered with A. Alfred Taubman, who started with Aurora Gasoline and later became a major mall developer. Fisher's public image and media savvy helped mask the decline of Detroit's industrial base, diverting attention to his lavish projects. His influence extended nationally, supporting the Republican Party and advising Presidents Eisenhower, Nixon, and Ford. He actively lobbied for Israeli policy goals, notably driving the 1973 Yom Kippur War weapons airlift and reconciliation efforts in 1975. He was recognized for his leadership in mobilizing support for Israel and was considered a "nexus" of an "old boys' network" including Taubman, Henry Ford II, and Leslie Wexner.

parts.title: Wexner's "Dybbuk" and the Genesis of His "Philanthropy"
parts.body: The chapter explores Leslie Wexner's public persona and his philanthropic efforts, particularly the Wexner Foundation. Wexner, a billionaire, gained media attention with profiles like the New York Magazine's "The Bachelor Billionaire." A striking aspect of these profiles was Wexner's description of his "dybbuk," a term from Jewish folklore for a disembodied, often malicious, spirit. Wexner described this "demon" as a part of his genius, compelling him to accumulate wealth and power, and keeping him emotionally stunted. This raised questions about how a man openly claiming to be guided by such an entity could have such a massive influence on Jewish communities. The Wexner Foundation, founded by Wexner and his mother Bella, aimed to develop stronger Jewish leadership in North America and Israel. Key figures in its establishment included Robert Hiller, a prominent nonprofit leader, and Rabbi Maurice Corson, who had ties to B'nai B'rith, a "Jewish fraternal organization" modeled as a secret society. Charles S. Liebman, an influential Jewish political scientist known for his controversial work on "Extremism as a Religious Norm," was also an early advisor. The Wexner Heritage Foundation, co-founded by Rabbi Herbert A. Friedman (who served in the Haganah, the precursor to the Israeli military), focused on strengthening volunteer leaders. Notably, the Wexner Foundation has direct and controversial ties to former Israeli head of state Ehud Barak, and its programs have molded generations of Jewish leaders, including many in AIPAC, which itself has controversial ties to Israeli intelligence.

parts.title: Israeli Espionage, the Mega Group, and Jeffrey Epstein's Alleged Role
parts.body: The text discusses Israeli espionage activities targeting the US, focusing on the "Mega Group" of billionaires connected to Israel and organized crime. Former Israeli intelligence official Ari Ben-Menashe alleged Epstein's sexual blackmail operation was created at Israel's behest to blackmail Clinton, suggesting Epstein's visits to the White House during a period of increased Israeli espionage. The document shifts to Hollinger International and Leslie Wexner's involvement. Wexner joined the board of this media company, founded by Conrad Black, who later defrauded the company. The board included prominent figures like Zbigniew Brzezinski, William Buckley, James Goldsmith, Lord Rothschild, Chaim Herzog, Paul Volcker, and Richard Perle. Perle, a key neo-conservative, co-authored "A Clean Break," advocating for regime change in Iraq and Syria, and had a controversial history of passing classified information to Israel. The Wexner Foundation funded a document, "Wexner Analysis: Israeli Communication Priorities 2003," linking US anti-terrorism efforts to Israeli policy goals, suggesting the Iraq War benefited Israeli interests. parts.title: Ghislaine Maxwell, the Kennedys, Robert Maxwell's Death, and the Rise of Jeffrey Epstein

His daughters Christine and Isabel, and Ghislaine herself, ventured into the internet business, creating the McKinley Group and Magellan search engine, with Ghislaine having a "substantial interest" and describing herself as an "internet operator." The narrative then shifts to Jeffrey Epstein's emergence as Ghislaine's benefactor and their public relationship, noting that Epstein's resemblance to Robert Maxwell was often highlighted, and some reports even suggested he, like Maxwell, might be working for Israeli intelligence and the CIA.

parts.title: The Fostergate Investigation and its Fallout
parts.body: The Fostergate investigation, led by Norman, uncovered major political figures, including Caspar Weinberger, who allegedly suppressed the story. Norman received an encrypted code, KPFBMMBODB, for a Swiss account which, after being accessed by a government employee, revealed $2.3 million in an account belonging to Weinberger. This money was linked to documents found in Barry Seal's car, suggesting Weinberger took kickbacks from drug and arms sales. Norman's investigation also implicated Mellon bank due to its donations to Malcolm Forbes' campaign and the pressure applied to kill Norman's story. Another Forbes editor, Dana Weschler Linden, had ties to Boston Systematics and the CIA through her father, Harry Weschler. After Norman's report was suppressed, J. Orlin Grabbe continued the investigation, corroborating much of Norman's work. Grabbe's findings included claims that Vince Foster stole Presidential authentication codes and nuclear options, selling them to Israel. He also alleged a Mossad agent was with Foster before his death and that a "Bush plumbers unit" was responsible, possibly due to Foster rejecting a $286,000 bribe. Grabbe reported an alleged confession from Robert Goetzman of the FBI, implicating him in Foster's death, which was recorded but seemingly ignored by Kenneth Starr. Despite being labeled a "misinformation" source by 60 Minutes, Grabbe's work suggested a broader conspiracy, involving 60 Minutes' Mike Wallace being paid by the DNC to discredit alternative narratives. This leads to a re-examination of the White House Historical Association fundraiser and its potential links to Systematics' money laundering or Foster and Clinton's alleged Israeli espionage, extending to China with Norman's "Oil Card" book.

parts.title: Epstein’s Enterprise and the Spook Airlines
parts.body: The text details how Jeffrey Epstein's White House visits and Bill Clinton's re-election campaign fundraising coincided with ventures involving Epstein, Leslie Wexner's The Limited, and CIA-linked airlines: Arrow Air and Southern Air Transport (SAT). In 1992, The Limited was involved in plans to make Rickenbacker Air Industrial Park a major cargo hub with Aeroflot, and critically, Arrow Air (identified in court documents as an Iran-Contra participant for moving weapons and equipment) was committed to daily flights connecting Latin America and Columbus. The first Aeroflot flight, carrying cargo for The Limited, occurred in April 1993, raising questions about the involvement of intelligence-linked airlines in Wexner's business. Following this, Southern Air Transport (SAT), also with ties to Iran-Contra and a former CIA lawyer as its owner, moved to Rickenbacker in 1995, largely to handle Hong Kong-to-Columbus cargo for The Limited. This relocation was heavily influenced by Wexner and facilitated by Ohio officials, offering substantial financial incentives. Key figures like former CIA chief Alan D. Fiers Jr. and Maj. Gen. Richard Secord (Iran-Contra coordinator) were involved in SAT's move. Local journalist Bob Fitrakis reported that Epstein was instrumental in courting SAT, with some officials suspecting Epstein and Wexner had CIA ties and that the cargo route was a "Meyer Lansky run" for organized crime money. SAT eventually went bankrupt amidst financial improprieties, and attention shifted to Lane Aviation Corp., which also had ties to Epstein and facilitated The Limited's flights. Later, lobbying by Wexner led to customs clearance for private planes at Rickenbacker, benefiting The Limited, and Landmark Aviation, another private terminal with Carlyle Group ownership (linked to intelligence and Epstein's associate David Rubenstein), also expanded operations there.

parts.title: Epstein's Exploitation of Modeling, Fashion, and Art Industries
parts.body: This chapter, "MODELING SCOUTS" and "VICTORIA'S SECRETS," focuses on Jeffrey Epstein's predatory tactics, particularly his exploitation of the modeling and fashion industries to find victims. His sex crimes reportedly began around 1985, coincidentally when he met Wexner and allegedly became associated with Robert Maxwell and Israeli intelligence. One key figure in his modeling schemes was Jean Luc Brunel, a model scout known for predatory behavior. Brunel, who co-founded Karin Models and later Next Models, was accused in a 1988 "60 Minutes" exposé of sexually assaulting underage girls and sabotaging careers of those who rejected his advances. Despite this, he later deepened his ties with Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell, with Epstein even providing Brunel with a $1 million line of credit for his modeling agency, MC2. Testimony from Brunel's bookkeeper and victim Virginia Roberts Giuffre suggests that MC2 models, often teenage girls from poor backgrounds, were housed in a property owned by Epstein's brother and then "loaned out to wealthy clients" for sexual exploitation. Epstein allegedly paid for their visas, and victims like Nadia Marcinkova were reportedly "purchased" from Eastern Europe. The chapter further details how Epstein and Maxwell used Victoria's Secret, owned by Epstein's associate Wexner, as a lure for aspiring models. Epstein often posed as a recruiter or even the owner of the brand, promising career advancement in exchange for sexual favors. This created what is described as an "Epstein-Victoria's Secret pimp pipeline." Even as early as 1993, a Victoria's Secret executive reported to the company's CEO, Les Wexner, that Epstein was misrepresenting himself as a recruiter, but Wexner allegedly did not stop him. Maxwell was also a frequent presence at Victoria's Secret events, reportedly acting as a "Nazi guard" and referring to young models as "pop tarts", suggesting her active involvement in the recruitment process. The section "GALLERINAS" also highlights Epstein and Maxwell's targeting of aspiring artists and musicians, referred to as "gallerinas." Maxwell would frequent high-end art galleries and auction houses like Sotheby's and Christie's, which had connections to Wexner, to find and recruit young women. Epstein also had ties to the New York Academy of Art, where he served on the board, and the Interlochen Centre for the Arts, where he established a scholarship lodge near a junior girls' camp. Victims from these institutions described being groomed with promises of scholarships or career help, only to be subjected to abuse or pressured to recruit others, including underage girls.

parts.title: BROKEN PROMISES
parts.body: Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell lured girls into their sex trafficking operation using promises of career boosts, money, and a better life. Victims like Carolyn (Minor Victim-4), who was only 14, were sexually abused and then financially incentivized to bring in other girls. Carolyn herself recruited three girls and was paid $600. Other victims were promised Harvard recommendations. Jane Doe #11 was raped after such a promise, and Marijke Chartouni was lured by Maxwell with tales of Epstein's wealth and connections. Virginia Roberts Giuffre was recruited at 16 with promises of travel and money if she "gave a wealthy man a massage." Some economically disadvantaged girls, like Haley Robson, who initially rejected Epstein's advances, were then groomed to become recruiters, bringing in "dozens of high-school girls from low income rural populations" for $200 per girl. Epstein even told Robson, "the younger the better." Some victims, like Jane Doe #9, were told that being sexually abused by Epstein was a form of "help." Ghislaine Maxwell played a crucial role in the operation, not only recruiting victims but also training them. She would feign friendship, show interest in their lives, and promise that Epstein could "help" them. Once in Epstein's residences, she would normalize outrageous behavior and erode their personal boundaries. Minor Victim-3 (Kate) detailed how Maxwell groomed her, making her wear a schoolgirl outfit and pushing her into sexual encounters with Epstein. Maxwell would ask if she had "fun" and praised her for compliance. Maxwell also referred to these underage girls as "trash" to her adult friends. Former employees described Maxwell as "the boss" and Epstein's "partner in business," managing the recruitment network and training victims in "massage" and sexual techniques. Maxwell even obtained a helicopter license to transport girls unseen, and victims often had their passports and phones seized. The operation was global in scope, targeting women and girls in Eastern Europe, Southeast Asia, and South America, beyond the domestic United States.

parts.title: Jeffrey Epstein's Global Travels with Bill Clinton and Ghislaine Maxwell: Unveiling Connections and Controversies
parts.body: The provided text discusses Jeffrey Epstein's trips with Bill Clinton and Ghislaine Maxwell to various countries, including Japan, Hong Kong, China, Singapore, Brunei, Thailand, and African nations. These trips, often on Epstein's private plane, involved meetings with heads of state, politicians, and business leaders. A significant event was a dinner in Singapore attended by Clinton, Epstein, and Maxwell, alongside Singapore's Prime Minister and other key figures, some of whom are now part of the World Economic Forum leadership. The text highlights Steven Green, then US ambassador to Singapore and a former corporate executive with ties to Leon Black, as a notable attendee. The narrative also touches upon the Sultan of Brunei's disturbing accusations of illegal sexual behavior, noting Epstein's indirect connections to him, including owning the building of Epstein's offices. Clinton and Epstein's paths diverged after Brunei, with Epstein continuing to Indonesia and Sri Lanka. Later trips by Clinton with Epstein and Maxwell to Asia are also mentioned, linking them to earlier discussions about Epstein's activities and Clinton White House scandals involving China. The Singapore visit is emphasized due to photographic evidence of Epstein and Maxwell with the head of state alongside Clinton, and suspicions surrounding Mark Middleton's activities in Singapore. The text then shifts to Clinton's Africa trip with Epstein in September 2002, which included celebrities Kevin Spacey and Chris Tucker. Other travelers included Clinton's advisor Doug Band and businessman Ron Burkle, who had a financial relationship with Clinton as an advisor to his company. Burkle's controversial past, including efforts to pardon Michael Milken, is detailed. Also on the trip was Casey Wasserman, an entertainment executive with familial ties to organized crime and a major donor to the Democratic Party and the LA Police Foundation. His family, the Wassermans, were significant political patrons of the Clintons. Other attendees included Rodney Slater, David Slang, and several women, some of whom are known Epstein accusers or are listed in his contact book. The trip's official purpose was to promote efforts to combat AIDS and encourage economic development in Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, Mozambique, and South Africa, involving meetings with local presidents and the launch of charitable initiatives. Epstein's claims of doing "lots of work in Africa" are linked to his potential continued involvement in Clinton's and Bill Gates' philanthropies focused on HIV/AIDS. The Africa trip concluded with a visit to Buckingham Palace, arranged by Prince Andrew, where Maxwell, Epstein, Clinton, and Spacey were present. The increasing public profile of Epstein due to these travels with Clinton is noted, along with Maxwell's growing influence within the Clinton philanthropies, including her accompanying Clinton on other trips without Epstein and her perceived role in fundraising. The text hints at a potential affair between Clinton and Maxwell.

parts.title: John Brockman's Literary and Tech Ventures
parts.body: John Brockman founded his literary agency in 1973, becoming known for his contacts and securing large advances. Despite criticisms from industry insiders about his methods, he's credited with making scientists' books marketable to the public and increasing their earnings. In the 1980s, Brockman expanded into the software industry, declaring himself the first "software agent." He angered figures like Bill Gates by "poaching" software authors. In 1985, he started the "Millionaires' Dinner," an annual event connecting Big Tech names with potential investors. This event, later called the "Billionaires' Dinner," facilitated major tech deals, but its purpose shifted as Silicon Valley's wealth grew more ostentatious.

parts.title: Chiliad, PROMIS, and the Evolution of Data-Driven Blackmail
parts.body: This text discusses Chiliad, a data analytics company co-founded by Christine Maxwell (Robert Maxwell's daughter), Paul McOwen, and Alan Wade (a CIA chief information officer). Chiliad was developed to provide tools for US intelligence and secured key contracts with the FBI after 9/11. Its software was remarkably similar to PROMIS software, raising concerns about intellectual property theft and an attempt to retool the software to avoid litigation. Wade and Maxwell's involvement, along with the software's similarity to PROMIS, suggests Chiliad may have been a successor to PROMIS, potentially carrying backdoors for foreign intelligence. Chiliad's funding included Allied Commercial Exporters Ltd. (linked to Jack Dellal, a British real estate mogul) and Hewlett-Packard, which had strong ties to US intelligence. Chiliad later shifted to healthcare data before folding, and Wade joined Darktrace, a UK cybersecurity firm with intelligence ties that focuses on healthcare data. This narrative connects to Palantir's rise, its own pivot to healthcare, and the broader theme of data as a valuable commodity and a tool for blackmail and mass surveillance. The text also details Jeffrey Epstein's efforts with Southern Trust to mine DNA data for profit and his suspected transition from sexual blackmail to electronic data blackmail, highlighting how digital footprints enable new forms of control and exploitation.
